lessons.title: Spacing: why the floor is wide
lessons.objective: See how shooters at the arc open lanes for everyone else.

payload.prompt: What does gravity mean in basketball?

options.text: A player's presence pulling defenders toward them, opening up teammates.
The downward force that makes shots arc.
How hard it is to jump on a tired defense.

explanation.correct: Right. A great shooter or scorer has gravity; defenders have to guard them closely, which leaves gaps and open teammates. The more gravity, the more the offense flows around them.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Gravity in basketball is about a player's presence on the court. A player with gravity pulls defenders toward them, freeing teammates.

payload.prompt: What happens to the driving lane when you space shooters around the arc?

options.text: Defenders have to help on shooters, leaving the lane more open for drives.
The lane gets narrower because there are more players outside.
Nothing changes; it is about shot selection.

explanation.correct: Exactly. When shooters are spread out, defenders cannot camp in the paint to help. The driving lanes stay open for the ball handler or cutters. This is why spacing and shooting are so valuable.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Spread shooters force defenders to guard them, which actually opens the driving lane more because fewer defenders can help in the paint.

payload.question: What is she talking about?

options.text: All five players are spread around the perimeter with good shooters, forcing defenders out.
The team is physically spread out on the bench.
They are taking only three-pointers.
The players are very tall.

payload.translation: Her team has multiple shooters positioned well around the court, stretching the defense and opening up driving lanes.

followUps.line: Yeah, they can score from anywhere.
followUps.why: You recognize that good spacing makes it hard to defend the whole court.

followUps.line: Who is their best three-point shooter?
followUps.why: A real follow-up that shows you are paying attention to who has gravity.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Good spacing means shooters are spread out. That is it.

lessons.title: Cuts and off-ball movement
lessons.objective: Recognize a backdoor cut and why moving without the ball matters.

payload.prompt: Match each cutting action to what it is.

pairs.definition: Quick movement toward basket to get open for a pass and finish.
Pass to teammate who cuts to basket for quick return pass and layup.
Cut where player breaks behind overplaying defender for an easy layup.

distractorDefinitions: A pass from the back of the court.
A screen set away from the ball.

explanation.summary: Core cutting actions: give-and-go is simplest play; backdoor cut beats overplaying defense.

payload.prompt: When is a backdoor cut most effective?

options.text: When a defender is overplaying a pass, so the cutter breaks behind them for an easy layup.
When the player has the ball in the corner.
When someone sets a screen.

explanation.correct: Right. A backdoor cut exploits a defender who is overcommitted to stopping a pass. The cutter slips behind and gets an open path to the basket because the defender is out of position.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A backdoor cut works when a defender is cheating to deny a pass, leaving the back open. It is a reaction to aggressive defense.

payload.prompt: Why is off-ball movement important to an offense?

options.text: It spreads the defense, creates scoring opportunities, and keeps defenders from helping on drives.
It scores points directly.
It gives the ball handler a chance to rest.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Players moving without the ball keep the defense moving and occupied. This spacing creates gaps, prevents help defense, and generates easy baskets.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Off-ball movement spreads the defense and creates lanes for everyone. Teammates without the ball must move to be effective.

payload.prompt: Tap the area where a cutter would receive a pass near the basket.

diagram.alt: A basketball court showing cutting lanes and areas near the basket.

hotspots.label: Near the basket on the cut

explanation.correct: Yes! A cutter gets the ball near the basket. The cut is most valuable when it gets you a close, easy scoring opportunity.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A cut is most effective when it gets the player near the basket for an easy finish. Distance from the rim matters.

payload.prompt: Tap an area where off-ball movement (movement without the ball) is happening.

diagram.alt: A basketball court showing offensive movement patterns.

explanation.correct: Right! Off-ball movement is any action taken by a teammate without the ball. This cutter is creating space and a scoring opportunity.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Off-ball movement is when a player moves WITHOUT the ball to create space or get open. A cutter moving to the basket is a perfect example.

payload.question: What is she talking about?

options.text: A player broke behind an overplaying defender for an easy basket.
Someone took a three-pointer.
A player traveled on the break.
The defense was not ready.

payload.translation: The offensive player caught the defender cheating and slipped behind them for an open, easy finish near the basket.

followUps.line: Yeah, the defender was overplaying the pass.
followUps.why: You recognize the defensive mistake that led to the cut being open.

followUps.line: Do they run that cut a lot?
followUps.why: A real follow-up asking whether this is part of their offensive system.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: A backdoor cut is just a player cutting behind a defender who is out of position.

lessons.title: Screens: the picks that free people
lessons.objective: Explain on-ball and off-ball screens in plain English.

payload.prompt: Match each screen type to its use.

pairs.definition: Screen for ball handler to create space for drive or shot.
Screen for player without ball to free them for catch-and-shoot or cut.
Credit for a screen that leads directly to a basket or assist.

distractorDefinitions: A pass that leads to a score.
A foul committed by a screen setter.

explanation.summary: Ball screens help handlers attack; off-ball screens free shooters. Both are fundamental.

payload.prompt: What does a ball handler do with a screen?

options.text: Uses it to create space for a drive, a jump shot, or to pass to an open teammate.
Passes the ball before the screen is set.
Always dunks over the defender.

explanation.correct: Exactly. A screen gives the ball handler space and options: drive to the rim, shoot a pull-up, or pass to the screener rolling or popping. It opens up the play.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A screen creates space for the ball handler to attack. They can drive, shoot or make a play depending on the defense's reaction.

payload.prompt: How is an off-ball screen different from a ball screen?

options.text: An off-ball screen frees a player WITHOUT the ball, usually for a catch-and-shoot.
Off-ball screens are always illegal.
Off-ball screens are only set by centers.

explanation.correct: Right. An off-ball screen is for a shooter or cutter who does not have the ball. It gets them open by the time they catch a pass. This is how teams free up their best shooters.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Off-ball screens free players without the ball for quick, open shots. They are legal and crucial for modern offense.

payload.prompt: Screener moves into defender's path after defense starts moving. Legal?

scene.alt: A screener initiating contact into a defender's path.

explanation.correct: Right. A screen is illegal if set into a defender's path after they're moving. Screener must be set first.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Illegal screens are set by moving into the defender's path. Screener must be stationary and not use elbows.

payload.prompt: The ball handler dribbles toward a teammate who sets a screen. Is a screen being used?

scene.alt: A dribbler approaching a teammate to use a screen.

choices.label: Yes, a ball screen is being set up.
No, this is just off-ball movement.

explanation.correct: Right. When the ball handler approaches a teammate for contact to create space, that is a ball screen. The screener is helping the ball handler.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. When the ball handler moves toward a teammate to use their body to create separation from their defender, that is a ball screen.

payload.prompt: A player sets a screen for a teammate who does not have the ball to get them open. Is this an off-ball screen?

scene.alt: A screen set for a player away from the ball.

choices.label: No, this is only a ball screen.

explanation.correct: Correct. Off-ball screens are for players without the ball. They are used to free shooters and cutters for easy scoring opportunities.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. If the screen is for a player without the ball, it is an off-ball screen by definition.

lessons.title: Shot types you will hear about
lessons.objective: Name layup, floater, pull-up, step-back, fadeaway, hook and dunk.

payload.prompt: Match each shot type to its description.

pairs.definition: Close-range shot from near the basket, usually bouncing off the backboard for high efficiency.
Soft, short-range jump shot inside the three-point line used by guards over defenders' hands.
Jump shot taken mid-dribble where the player pulls up suddenly to create shooting space.

distractorDefinitions: A shot with a very high arc.

explanation.summary: These three are workhorses of offense: layups for efficiency, floaters for guards, pull-ups for creating space.

payload.prompt: Match each advanced shot type to what it does.

pairs.definition: Dribbler steps back away from defender to create space for a jump shot.
Shooter moves away from defender while shooting to create distance and make blocking harder.
Post-player move where ball extends away from body in an arc. Less common in modern game.

distractorDefinitions: A shot blocked by the rim.

explanation.summary: Advanced shots: step-back and fadeaway create space; hooks are post moves seen less in modern ball.

payload.prompt: What is a catch-and-shoot player?

options.text: A player who receives a pass and shoots immediately without dribbling, usually a specialist in perimeter shooting.
A player who steals the ball and scores.
A player who catches a rebound and dunks.

explanation.correct: Right. Catch-and-shoot players are efficient because they do not waste time dribbling; they just catch and fire. They are usually role players or sharpshooters.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Catch-and-shoot is about shooting immediately after catching a pass. These players are efficient and valuable for spacing an offense.

payload.prompt: What is an alley-oop?

options.text: A pass to a teammate who dunks or lays it in in mid-air before landing.
A rebound by the team that just missed.
An assist from the point guard.

explanation.correct: Exactly. An alley-oop is a lob pass to a teammate who finishes near the rim, usually with a dunk. It is an easy, high-percentage play.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. An alley-oop is a lob pass that a teammate finishes by dunking or laying it in. It is a spectacular but high-percentage play.

payload.prompt: Complete the shot descriptions.
payload.template: A {{layup-term}} is a close-range shot near the basket. A {{catch-term}} player receives a pass and shoots immediately without dribbling.

explanation.correct: Perfect. Layups are highest-percentage; catch-and-shoot players are efficient role players.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A layup is near-rim and high efficiency. Catch-and-shoot is immediate shooting after catching.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: He can not take a pull-up on the move.

payload.question: What is she saying about him?

options.text: He cannot shoot accurately when dribbling and stopping for a jump shot.
He cannot run fast.
He cannot jump high.
He is not allowed to move.

payload.translation: She is saying his shooting mechanics or decision-making breaks down when he tries to take a jump shot while dribbling. It is a weakness.

followUps.line: Yeah, he has to get set to shoot.
followUps.why: You are recognizing that he needs to be stationary for accurate shots.
Good question about whether defenders take advantage of this limitation.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: A pull-up is just shooting while dribbling. It takes practice.

lessons.title: Shot quality: rim, three, free throw
lessons.objective: Estimate why the rim and the arc beat the long two.

payload.prompt: What percentage of a team's shots should come from three or at the rim (not the midrange)?

explanation.correct: Exactly right. Modern teams shoot around 75% of their shots from three-pointers or layups because these shots are most efficient. The midrange is dead.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Elite modern teams shoot three-pointers and rim shots almost 75% of the time. The midrange is avoided because it is inefficient.

payload.prompt: How many three-pointers per game does an NBA team attempt now?

explanation.correct: Spot on. Modern NBA teams attempt around 33 three-pointers per game, triple what they attempted 20 years ago. This is the three-point revolution.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. NBA teams now attempt around 33 three-pointers per game on average, a huge increase from earlier eras.

payload.prompt: Which type of shot (rim, three, or midrange) most often leads to free throws?

explanation.correct: Right. Driving to the rim (around 75% of cases when a foul occurs) leads to free throws more often than perimeter shots. This is why attacking the rim is valuable.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Shots at the rim lead to fouls and free throws far more often than three-pointers or midrange attempts, which is another reason to attack inside.

payload.prompt: Tap the area where midrange shots are (between the paint and the three-point line).

diagram.alt: A basketball court showing different shooting zones.

explanation.correct: Yes! The midrange is the zone between the paint and the three-point line, roughly 10-22 feet. This is the zone modern teams avoid because the efficiency is lowest.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The midrange is the area between the paint and the three-point arc. It is inefficient in the modern game.

payload.prompt: Tap the corner three-point area (shortest three-pointer).

diagram.alt: A basketball court showing corner three-point zones.

explanation.correct: Exactly! Corner threes are the shortest three-pointers (22 ft instead of 23'9") and the most efficient. Teams hunt corner threes.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The corner three is the shortest three-point distance at 22 feet in the NBA, making it the most efficient and highly coveted shot.

payload.prompt: What changed basketball when teams started taking more three-pointers?

options.text: Defenses had to spread out to guard perimeter shooters, opening driving lanes and changing how offense is structured.
Games became slower.
Only tall players can play now.

explanation.correct: Right. The three-point revolution forced defenses to guard shooters at distance, which opened the lane for drives and cutters. It transformed how offense is played.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. More three-pointers means defenses have to space out and guard the perimeter, opening up the interior for drives and cuts. This is the core of modern offense.

lessons.title: Passing and playmaking
lessons.objective: Tell an assist from a hockey assist and a skip pass from a swing.

payload.prompt: Match each pass type to what it does.

pairs.definition: Pass to teammate who directly scores. Official scorer credits this if it leads to basket.
Pass to teammate who passes to scorer. Also called assist-on-assist; not official but fans notice.
Short, quick bounce pass to rolling or cutting teammate. Precise, common in pick-and-roll.

explanation.summary: Official assists vs hockey assists show vision; pocket passes are tight, efficient passes.

payload.prompt: When is a pocket pass most useful?

options.text: On a pick-and-roll, to get the ball to the screener rolling to the basket quickly and precisely.
When shooting a three-pointer.
On a fast break from mid-court.

explanation.correct: Exactly. A pocket pass is the signature pass in a pick-and-roll, getting the ball to the roller's hands at the right moment for a layup or score.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Pocket passes are tight, efficient passes used often on screens. The most common use is the roll pass on a pick-and-roll.

payload.prompt: What is a skip pass?

options.text: A long pass across the court that skips over intermediate defenders to find an open shooter.
A pass that bounces on the floor.
A pass to a teammate who does not catch it.

explanation.correct: Right. A skip pass goes from one side of the court to the opposite side, often from the ball handler to a wing or corner shooter. It is used when help defense collapses.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A skip pass is a long cross-court pass that finds an open shooter on the opposite side after the defense over-helps one side.

payload.prompt: What is the goal of a drive-and-kick?

options.text: Drive toward the rim to collapse the defense, then kick out to an open teammate for a three-pointer.
Drive to the basket and score.
Pass to a teammate who drives.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Drive-and-kick is a fundamental offensive action: the driver creates space by attacking, draws defenders, and passes to an open shooter. It is high-percentage and common.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Drive-and-kick is about drawing defenders in by driving, then kicking out to an open perimeter shot. It is one of the most important plays.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: He has seven assists and only two turnovers.

payload.question: What does this tell you about his play?

options.text: He is making good decisions, creating scoring for teammates, and not losing the ball much.
He is not shooting enough.
He is playing defense.
He is tired.

payload.translation: He is being a great playmaker: passing the ball to open teammates who score, while protecting the ball and avoiding turnovers. This is elite play.

followUps.why: You are recognizing his ability to see and make passes others miss.

followUps.line: Who did he get most of his assists to?
followUps.why: A real follow-up that shows you are paying attention to who is benefiting.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Good assist-to-turnover ratio means smart, unselfish play.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: That play had some nice hockey assists.

payload.question: What is she noticing?

options.text: Multiple passes led to the basket, showing good ball movement and assists-on-assists.
Someone played hockey before basketball.
The team scored multiple times.
The defense made mistakes.

payload.translation: The possession featured multiple passes before the basket, showing good ball movement. Each passer contributed to the score even if only the last passer gets credited with an official assist.

followUps.why: You are recognizing unselfish, team-oriented offense.

followUps.line: That is how they should always play.
followUps.why: A comment on their system and philosophy.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Hockey assists are passes that lead to the assist. Fans love seeing ball movement.

lessons.title: Post play and isolation
lessons.objective: Explain a post-up, an isolation and why mismatches get hunted.

payload.prompt: What is a post-up?

options.text: Receiving the ball in the low or high post (elbow or block) with the back to the basket, then attacking from there.
A pass to someone on the perimeter.
A foul called near the basket.

explanation.correct: Right. A post-up puts a big man in position to back down their defender, use fakes, or pass to cutters. It is a fundamental offensive action.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A post-up is an offensive set where a player (usually a big) receives the ball in the post with their back to the basket, then makes a move.

payload.prompt: What is an isolation (iso) play?

options.text: An offensive set where one player attacks their defender one-on-one while teammates stay out of the way.
A defensive formation.
A time out called by a coach.

explanation.correct: Exactly. An iso is when a player, usually a star scorer, gets space to go one-on-one against their defender. Used late in the shot clock or in clutch situations.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Isolation is about giving a player space to attack their defender alone. Teammates clear out to let the star go to work.

payload.prompt: A big man is guarding a smaller guard who shoots threes. Is this a mismatch?

explanation.correct: Right. When a guard has a size advantage (speed, range) and the big man does not, it is a mismatch the offense exploits by attacking or shooting.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. If a big man cannot guard a guard's three-point shooting or speed, it is a mismatch that the offense should attack.

payload.prompt: Your best player is double-teamed in the final seconds. What should they do?

options.text: Pass to an open teammate; double-teams create opportunities elsewhere.
Force a shot through the double-team coverage.
Dribble into traffic trying to escape.

explanation.correct: Right. When doubled, one of your other teammates is open. Passing is faster and better than dribbling out.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A double-team forces passing because teammates become open. Shooting or dribbling into traffic is inefficient.

payload.prompt: You spot the opponent's center is too slow for your forward. What do you do?

options.text: Hunt the mismatch by targeting your forward against the center every possession.
Avoid passing to the forward to keep the mismatch hidden.
Pass to your worst player instead.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Hunting mismatches is core to modern basketball. Target advantages relentlessly until defense adjusts.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Mismatches are gold in basketball. Attack them every possession to exploit the size or speed advantage.

payload.question: What does this mean?

options.text: Late in the game, the team is letting one player attack one-on-one.
The team is playing isolation defense.
A player is isolated on the bench.
The team is isolated from fans.

payload.translation: In the final moments of the game, the team is running isolation plays to let their best player attack their defender one-on-one for a crucial shot or score.

followUps.line: Yeah, give him space to create.
followUps.why: You recognize that iso plays are about letting a star go to work.

followUps.line: Can he get a bucket against that defender?
followUps.why: Real follow-up about whether he can win the one-on-one matchup.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Iso ball is just giving one player space to attack. Simple concept.
